issues.description: The problem statement and the template define Course.instructor as a String, but the solution's Course implementation uses instructor of type [String]. Additionally, the solution's Client constructs a Course using a String instructor, which conflicts with the solution Course initializer signature. This cross-artifact type mismatch for the instructor property will confuse students about the expected type and prevents a consistent implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the instructor type consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) change the solution's Course to use instructor: String and adjust any code that treats it as an array, or (B) update the problem statement and template to declare instructor as [String] and update the Client to pass an array of instructor names (e.g. ["Matthias", "Patrick", "Felix"]). Prefer option (A) if the intended exercise text should remain unchanged (single String instructor).

issues.description: The conceptual property 'instructor' on the Course entity is represented as a String in the problem statement and the template, but the solution defines it as [String] (an array). This divergence in the representation of the same conceptual attribute creates a mismatch students must resolve and can cause compilation/usage confusion (the Client in the problem expects a single String instructor).
issues.suggestedFix: Align the representation of Course.instructor across artifacts. Preferably change the solution to use instructor: String (update the property, initializer parameter, and usages) so it matches the problem statement and template. Alternatively, if multiple instructors are intended, update the problem statement and template to describe instructor as [String] and adjust the Client example to pass an array.
